title: Tool brand sourcing in China
summary: An EU-based, listed brand and importer of power tools and garden equipment with its own battery platform. Products are made by around 200 suppliers in mainland China and sold mainly to consumers in the EU, with further markets in North America and Australia. The reader works on sustainability with those suppliers.
facts: More than 1,000 employees and more than €450m turnover, so inside the CSRD scope after Omnibus I
Fewer than 5,000 employees, so outside the direct scope of the CSDDD
Sells under its own brand, which makes it the manufacturer in the sense of EU product law even though suppliers build the products
Imports finished, packaged goods; does not import raw steel, aluminium or other basic materials

batteries.why: The battery platform makes this the most demanding product law for the business.
points: Selling batteries under your own brand makes you the manufacturer: conformity assessment, CE marking, labelling and from 18 February 2027 the QR code are your responsibility, whoever builds the pack.
Tool battery packs are portable batteries. They need no battery passport; that applies to light-means-of-transport, industrial and electric-vehicle batteries.
From 18 February 2027 portable batteries built into products must be removable and replaceable by the end user. Removable packs meet this by design; products with built-in cells need a design check.

Raw-material due diligence applies from 18 August 2027 to operators above €40m turnover: a verified policy for cobalt, lithium, nickel and natural graphite, which means mapping the chain behind your cell suppliers.
Producer registration and take-back are organised country by country.
ask: Cell manufacturer and model for every pack, and the cell maker's sources of cobalt, lithium, nickel and graphite
Carbon footprint and recycled-content data from the cell maker, even where not yet mandatory for portable batteries
Design confirmation that built-in batteries can be removed with common tools

forced-labour.why: The ban covers every product and every importer from 14 December 2027, and attention on supply chains in China is high.
points: Authorities carry the burden of proof, but the first thing they ask is what you do to identify and address forced labour risks. Documented due diligence is the practical defence.
Risk sits deeper than tier 1: battery materials, aluminium, cotton in gloves and workwear, polysilicon in solar products.
A banned product must be withdrawn and disposed of at your cost, in all Member States.
Evidence gathering in China has legal limits of its own; see the entry on Chinese audit and data rules.
ask: Names and locations of sub-suppliers for the inputs with known risk
Recruitment and labour-transfer practices, including use of labour agencies
Agreement to audits and to sharing the results

csrd.why: The group reports under the CSRD, and much of the value-chain information comes from your suppliers.
points: Purchased goods dominate the group's Scope 3 emissions, so supplier energy and emissions data are the core of the climate disclosure.
Working conditions at suppliers are reported under the standard on value-chain workers, drawing on your audit findings.
The value-chain cap protects suppliers with up to 1,000 employees: you may not require more from them than the voluntary standard contains. Larger suppliers are not protected.
The German transposition law is the legal basis for the group's report; see CSRD in Germany.
ask: Energy use by source and production volume, per factory and year
Headcount, working hours, wages against the local minimum and accident figures
Existing certificates and audit reports, to avoid asking twice

esrs.why: The standards define which supplier data the group needs for reports up to financial year 2026.
points: The topics that involve suppliers most are climate (E1), resource use and circular economy (E5), workers in the value chain (S2) and business conduct (G1).
Estimates are allowed where supplier data cannot be obtained with reasonable effort; say where you used them.

esrs-revised.why: From financial year 2027 your supplier data requests should follow the revised, shorter standards.
points: Fewer datapoints means you can shorten supplier questionnaires. Remove what is no longer required.
Use the voluntary standard as the template for suppliers with up to 1,000 employees; it is the legal ceiling for what you may require from them.
Decide with group reporting whether 2026 data is collected under Set 1 or the revised standards.
ask: The data points of the voluntary standard, in one yearly request

ppwr.why: Every product you sell is packaged, and as the brand owner you answer for that packaging.
points: The general rules apply since 12 August 2026, including limits on PFAS in food-contact packaging and the duty to hold technical documentation.
From 2030 packaging must be at least 70% recyclable and plastic packaging needs recycled content; redesign takes time with 200 suppliers.
Empty space in shipping and e-commerce packaging is limited to 50%. Blister packs and oversized boxes are the usual problems.
Producer registration and fees are national: one per Member State you sell into.
ask: Packaging specification per product: materials, weights, coatings, inks and adhesives
Recycled content with evidence
Declarations on PFAS and heavy metals

espr.why: Product requirements for your categories are not set yet, but two rules already apply and more are planned.
points: As a large company you must disclose each year how many unsold consumer products you discarded and why.
Horizontal rules on repairability and on recycled content of electrical equipment are in the working plan; they would reach power tools before any tool-specific act.
A Digital Product Passport will come with each delegated act. The data behind it, such as materials and repair information, has to come from suppliers.
ask: Bills of materials with material types and weights
Spare-part availability and disassembly information

right-to-repair.why: Vacuum cleaners and welding equipment are on the list of products that must be repaired on request, and the liability extension covers everything you sell to consumers.
points: For listed products you must offer repair at a reasonable price for as long as the ecodesign rules require spare parts, also after the guarantee has ended.
You may not block repair through contract terms, hardware or software.
When a consumer chooses repair under the legal guarantee, liability is extended by 12 months. This applies to all consumer goods sold on or after 31 July 2026.
Cordless tools in general are not on the list yet. It grows as ecodesign acts add repairability requirements.
ask: Guaranteed spare-part supply for the required number of years, with prices
Repair manuals and exploded drawings

rohs.why: Electrical tools are in scope, and the proof comes from your suppliers' materials.
points: Compliance is part of the CE marking: you need technical documentation showing that each homogeneous material meets the limits.
Common weak points are lead in solder and in brass or aluminium alloys, phthalates in cables and soft grips, and cadmium in pigments.
Several exemptions for lead in alloys are time-limited. If a product relies on one, follow its expiry date.
ask: Material declarations for every component, backed by test reports for high-risk parts
Notice of any change of material or sub-supplier

reach.why: As the EU importer of finished goods you are responsible for the substances in them.
points: If any component contains a substance of very high concern above 0.1% by weight, you must inform business customers, answer consumers within 45 days and notify the SCIP database.
The Candidate List grows twice a year. Supplier declarations therefore go out of date and need a refresh after each update.
Restrictions in Annex XVII bite on typical tool parts: PAHs in rubber and plastic grips, lead, cadmium, phthalates.
A broad PFAS restriction would affect seals, lubricants, coatings and battery components.
ask: A declaration against the current Candidate List for every article, renewed after each update
Test reports for grips, cables and coated parts

machinery.why: Every power tool placed on the EU market from 20 January 2027 must meet the new regulation.
points: There is no transition period for new stock: declarations of conformity and technical files must refer to the regulation from that date.
Importers get explicit duties: check the manufacturer's documentation, add your contact details, keep the declaration for ten years.
Instructions may be digital, but consumers must receive the safety information on paper.
Circular saws and chainsaws are on the list of machinery with stricter conformity assessment; harmonised standards remain the usual route.
ask: Updated risk assessments and technical files against the regulation
A plan for which production batches switch to the new declaration

ecgt.why: You advertise to consumers, so every environmental claim on packaging, websites and in catalogues falls under the new bans.
points: Generic claims such as ‘eco’ or ‘sustainable’ are banned without recognised excellent performance. Check packaging artwork that suppliers prepare.
Self-made sustainability logos are banned; labels need a certification scheme behind them.
Durability and battery-life claims must be provable, and repairability may not be overstated.
A commercial durability guarantee of more than two years may use the new harmonised label.
ask: Evidence for any environmental or durability claim that originates from the supplier

cn-audit-rules.why: These rules shape what you can ask, record and send abroad when you collect supplier evidence in China.
points: Questionnaires and audits that single out particular regions or groups can be seen as implementing foreign measures against China, which the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law allows authorities to counter.
Worker interviews, ID copies and payroll records are personal information. Collecting them and sending them to headquarters needs a legal basis under the Personal Information Protection Law.
Audit and investigation firms have come under scrutiny; choose providers that are properly licensed in China.
Get legal advice in China on the wording of supplier documents and on data transfers. The aim is to meet EU expectations without creating a breach of Chinese law for you or the supplier.

de-csrd.why: This act is the legal basis for the group's sustainability report in Germany.
points: Until it is in force, the group reports under the older rules on the non-financial statement and applies the ESRS voluntarily.
Once in force, the report becomes part of the management report and is audited with limited assurance, so supplier data needs an evidence trail.

csddd.why: The group is below the 5,000-employee threshold, but large retail customers are in scope and pass requirements on.
points: Expect contract clauses, codes of conduct and questionnaires from customers that are in scope. They may only ask smaller partners for information they need and cannot get otherwise.
Germany will transpose the directive one-to-one and replace the LkSG with it, so the German threshold is set to rise to 5,000 employees.
Its logic is still the benchmark for your own supplier programme: risk-based, focused on the most severe and most likely harm, engagement before disengagement.
ask: The same evidence you need for the forced labour ban and for customer requests; collect it once

de-lksg.why: Whether it binds the group directly depends on having at least 1,000 employees in Germany; German retail customers under the act pass its requirements on either way.
points: Check the headcount in Germany, including temporary agency workers employed for more than six months. Staff of foreign subsidiaries do not count.
The duties themselves continue while the reporting duty is being abolished: risk analysis, preventive measures at direct suppliers, a complaints procedure.
The announced narrowing to the CSDDD thresholds would take the group out of scope. Until a law is passed, the current text applies.

cbam.why: Finished tools are not CBAM goods today, but the extension to steel- and aluminium-intensive products from 2028 could bring some of them in.
points: The Commission proposed about 180 downstream products; the Council and Parliament want longer lists. The final annex decides, by customs code.
Check the customs codes of your products against the annex as soon as the text is agreed.
If products are covered, you need the embedded emissions of their steel and aluminium, which your suppliers must obtain from their material suppliers.
ask: Weight of steel and aluminium per product
Origin and producer of the steel and aluminium used

eudr.why: Complete tools are not covered, but some wooden and rubber items sold separately could be.
points: Scope is decided by customs code. A garden tool with a wooden handle is classified as a tool and is outside; wooden handles or other wooden articles imported as such can be inside.
Packaging that only carries another product is not covered.
If an item is covered, you as the importer are the operator and need geolocation data for the wood.
ask: For any wooden article sold as such: species and country and plot of harvest

conflict-minerals.why: The duty rests on importers of the metals, not on importers of products that contain them.
points: Tools contain tin in solder and small amounts of gold and tantalum in electronics. Customers and rating agencies may ask for smelter information.

taxonomy.why: The group reports Taxonomy figures, but they are prepared by finance and involve suppliers very little.
points: Trading and manufacturing of tools is mostly not described in the Taxonomy, so reported shares are low by design.

ets.why: The group runs no installations under the ETS. ETS2 will raise fuel costs for logistics and buildings in the EU from 2028.

cn-ets.why: Tool factories are not covered, but their steel, aluminium and power suppliers are.
points: A carbon price paid in China can be deducted under CBAM, so it matters if your products come into the CBAM scope.
Suppliers of covered materials will have verified emissions data, which improves what your suppliers can report to you.

cn-csds.why: It tells you which of your suppliers will publish sustainability data of their own.
points: Listed suppliers in the main indices already publish reports; these are a ready source for your data requests.
The standards are moving from voluntary to mandatory by 2030 and from large to smaller companies, so supplier readiness will improve.

green-claims.why: The proposal is stalled. The binding rules on claims are in the ECGT directive.

pay-transparency.why: It binds the group as an employer in the EU and is handled by HR, not through suppliers.

sfdr.why: It applies to investors. They use the group's reported data.

green-bond.why: Relevant only if the group issues a green bond.

esg-ratings.why: It regulates the rating providers. As a listed company the group is rated and now has a right to check the facts a rating is based on.
